With their truck gone, the team fights on - repossessing a van, facing a wild baker.
With Matt onboard, the team repos a rich kid's ride, an "Uncle Sam" vehicle, and battles rowdy rugby players.
Take a look inside the fast-paced, high pressure world of car repossession with highly trained professionals.
The confusion over Lou's new business relationship with Matt continues to mount.
The new truck arrives, fueling the growing feud between Team Lou and Team Matt.
After Froy's injury on a repo, tensions between Lou and Matt reach new heights.

Tensions between Lou and Matt continue to boil when Matt enlists his daughter's aid on another job.
A new rift between Matt and the rest of the crew puts the fate of the team in question.
On this season finale, Matt and Lou have their final confrontation and the team loses a member.

Sonia's recovery takes another unexpected turn when she goes too far with a debtor.
Things get a lot more complicated for the team when Sonia puts herself on the business end of a knife.

The team gets back to work, but have their anger management sessions had any effect?
The team's work with the anger management specialist starts to pay off with disastrous consequences.
Matt and Froy crash a meeting to ask for a car, but instead they get an angry old man with a rifle.
Sonia and Froy disrupt a wild debtor, clash with workers, and face a repo that ends in destruction.

Sonia and Matt go to a garden center to repo a forklift, but a language barrier causes chaos.
With the pressure of Froy's legal problems mounting, the team tries to convince him to hire a lawyer.
Froy meets with a lawyer, but his legal troubles are worse than expected.
While Froy waits on news from his lawyer, he considers taking matters into his own hands.
Matt and Froy head to Texas to clear Froy's name, but things take a turn for the worse.
When a debtor and his friends resort to baseball bats, chaos erupts.
Down in Texas, Matt and Froy are staking out a cement mixer, but their repo turns disastrous.
First, Frankie and Lyndah find themselves in a fancy neighborhood, dealing with a pair of uptight yuppies.
Matt and Froy face incredible odds against a Texas-sized biker gang looking for a beat down.
Matt and Froy set out to repo a truck from a wealthy Texan.

Josh expects a bounty for bringing in Daniel Trenner but his prisoner is stolen by the sheriff. Ex-army personnel want to stage an illegal trial accusing their former lieutenant of dereliction of duty
Josh is hired by a woman to sober up Harry, a drunk who is also Josh's friend. She learned his wealthy brother who Harry hasn't seen in years is coming to visit so she wants Harry to be presentable.
Josh and the beautiful prisoner he is transporting are on a three day trip while her partner is still on the loose. For once Josh may not follow through on obeying the law as they fall in love.

Josh is on his way to River City to transport three convicts there to be hanged. The dangerous prisoners escape and appoint themselves the law, after the town is hit by a tornado, killing the sheriff.
A journalist accompanies Josh on his manhunt to get an exclusive story on a bounty hunter. Josh agrees to let him join him in the hunt for Jack Torrance but finds they have different methods.

Josh feels compelled to repay a debt to an old friend who's in jail and may hang. However, the friend escapes, forcing Josh to go on the hunt for him until it appears he died when he went over a cliff
Josh brings in outlaw Carlos Domingo, but he has to be released when the witness against him is killed. Josh concocts a surprise witness to testify against the notorious killer - his own mother.
Josh is sent for by the desperate men of Coronado. He is hired to convince the women of the town to come back to their men when they leave demanding that all towns men give up their guns for good.

Josh brings in a man wanted for robbery but loses his reward. A well meaning doctor pays an innocent man to take the blame for his son, but the son sets out to kill the man to make sure he never tells
Josh arrives in a town for rest just as the local bank has been robbed. A traveling medicine man knows the whereabouts of the suspect and wants Josh to help because he thinks the suspect is innocent.
A widow wants to hire/propose to Josh so she doesn't lose custody of her son. Josh served under her husband in the war. His mother now is trying to steal her grandson to take over the family fortune.
A woman asks Josh, an old friend, to help find her husband Frank - a bounty hunter out to settle a score. He wants to catch a young outlaw who shot him in the leg.
When Randall has a sheriff bed a prisoner, the man's gang kidnaps the sheriff and two others and threatens to kill one per day until the man is freed.
In Mexico, Josh is hired to protect a man and his pregnant wife from his the villagers who are angered when he refuses the town healing woman or "witch" from being present when his wife gives birth.
After Josh takes the task of finding a man and his wife's pet ewe, he becomes the butt of many jokes while cattlemen nearly hang him when he mentions sheep. His only clue is a gold bell the ewe wore.
When a convicted killer escapes prison, Josh is hired to protect the woman whose testimony put him there. The woman's husband is a lawyer who says he has always been a coward and never carries a gun.
Josh rides into a town looking for a man who wants to hire him. When he goes to the man's room at the hotel, Josh is shot. He must figure out who shot him but the sheriff is ordering him out of town.
Josh is hired by Harry Weaver to track down his twin brother Pete, a wanted man. Harry is tired of being used by Pete, plus the law and bounty hunters are apt to mistake him for Pete.

Josh is called in to track down a new outlaw, the local sheriff who is a friend. The good sheriff who was seduced into robbing a bank by his girlfriend, convinces Josh to let him assist in her capture
Josh takes a job protecting a deaf teenage girl and keeping everyone off the father's place for a day or two. Although initially bored, Josh starts to develop a relationship with the friendly girl.
Josh escorts a photographer to take a picture of his friend El Gato, who is a hilarious bandit living in the hills of Mexico with a small army. However, El Gato is new to photographs and leery.
A broke Josh is hired by a fearful man to help him elope with his sweetheart, Jane, the daughter of a local rancher. The girl's father is vehemently opposed to the marriage.

Josh takes a job protecting an express office employee who stole $10,000 and wants to return it before it's discovered missing. However, he had an accomplice and does not know where the accomplice is.
A Japanese woman travels to the U.S. to find a man who proposed to her and hires Josh to find him since no one will help her. Josh is confronted by the Japanese man to whom she had been promised.
Josh arrives in town thinking the sheriff summoned him to go after a man. Instead, a woman wants Josh to bring in the man, her wanted husband, alive, so he can prove self defense.
Josh rides to Barney Durant's horse business right after Barney pushes his son to leave. When Josh's prisoners escape taking 2 horses from his horse trader friend, he helps in tracking them down.
While pursuing Carl Martin, Josh stops at a marshal's office and is falsely accused of the marshal's murder.
When phony wanted posters seek a retired Confederate officer, Colonel Sykes' daughter summons Josh to help.
An old man with an Apache bodyguard is wanted for a crime committed long ago.

A banker hires Randall to track down the man he believes responsible for his son's death and a bank robbery.
Randall must transport a killer to Tucson, but exchanges him for the nun kidnapped by the killer's gang.

Josh sets out to help a wife locate her missing husband, but his mission meets with a resistant townspeople.

Will is uneasy about the whole idea of Grace marrying Leo (guest star Harry Connick Jr.). Debbie Reynolds and Katie Couric also guest star.
Will invites Karen to move in with him after she is kicked out of the Plaza Hotel; Elton John is an all-seeing arbiter of gay style.
Grace has only two tickets to "The Nutcracker" and cannot decide whether to take Will or Leo. Mary McDonough guest stars.
Jack convinces Will to join a gay soccer team; Karen is giddy in anticipation of her date with a handsome restaurateur (Andy Garcia).
Grace is puzzled by her new neighbor -- a bizarre bohemian woman.
Will and Jack coach Karen's cousin (Dan Futterman) on his new gay lifestyle, reminding Will of his own experience of coming out in 1986.
Karen's rival (Minnie Driver) attempts to manipulate Jack; Will and Grace revitalize their friendship with a night of board games.
Jack encounters his former babysitter (guest star Demi Moore) and lapses into childlike behavior. Rosanna Arquette and Leigh-Allyn Baker also guest star.
Will and Jack's transformation of Karen's cousin Barry is complete; Karen duels with Beverly during a silent auction for charity.
Jealous Will spots Barry (Dan Futterman) disappearing with Jack; Karen trades places with Rosario to woo a handsome handyman (Bruno Campos).
Will forms an anti-romance club with Karen and his boss (Gene Wilder).
Will attempts to surprise Grace for her birthday by sneaking Leo back from Africa; Jack and Karen take their mission to keep Leo's return secret too seriously.
Karen's search for a roommate leads to a high-maintenance individual, who shares many of her eccentricities; Grace and Jack intervene when Will uses painkillers as a crutch.
Karen hires a somewhat immature divorce attorney (guest star Macaulay Culkin) to oppose Will in court.
When Karen's ex-husband dies, she and her British rival (Minnie Driver) have a contest of wills; Leo (Harry Connick Jr.) is needed in Guatemala.
Karen confronts her ex-husband's mistress before inviting everybody for a ceremony on her yacht; Grace suffers from jealousy after meeting her husband's sexy co-worker.
Will and Jack awake in a precarious position while at sea; Grace discovers love letters in Leo's bag from a female colleague.
Grace is vexed when she learns that Leo's ex-girlfriend (Mira Sorvino) is intimately acquainted with Will.
Karen invites Grace and Leo to play tennis at her exclusive club, but her fierce playing style drives Grace away.
Jack lands a speaking role opposite James Earl Jones in an off-Broadway play and gives the veteran actor some pointers.
Will takes Leo on shopping sprees and for high tea to help him rekindle his love of the city; Karen coaches Jack for the annual gay spelling bee.
Will takes his mother for an afternoon stroll and bumps into an attractive bachelor (Dylan McDermott); Karen continues her lifelong quest to hunt down hubby-stealing Lorraine.
An unorthodox doctor (Jack Black) gives Karen her annual physical; Jack begs Will to support his decision to become a student nurse.
Will urges Grace to stay in New York so they can spend some time together; Karen strong-arms Jack's nursing teacher into letting him skip class but still make the grade.
Will catches the eye of a female diner after being stood up; Grace bumps into a man (Tom Everett Scott) with whom she once shared a forgettable encounter; Karen runs into her nemesis, Candice Bergen.

A weak bladder forces Will to entrust Grace with his place in line for Barry Manilow tickets; Grace's mother (Debbie Reynolds) cancels their annual mother-daughter shopping trip to have dinner with Jack.

Grace's freeloading sister (Geena Davis) comes to town to launch her latest business enterprise; Karen spurns Lyle (John Cleese), then changes her mind after Lorraine (Minnie Driver) expresses her disapproval.
A rich plastic surgeon (guest star Hal Linden) tries to buy Will's affection; Grace boycotts a new restaurant.
Will's new client (Dave Foley) falls for Jack; Grace and Karen discover hidden money while trying to fix the plumbing in Leo's cabin.
Will is the only single man in a cooking class full of couples, including Jack and his new boyfriend (Dave Foley); Karen's mother (Suzanne Pleshette) asks Grace to decorate her apartment.
Will and Grace begin a business venture selling apartments; Jack runs into his former acting mentor, Zandra; Karen and Lyle (John Cleese) try to renew romance.
Will and Grace try to break up Jack and Stuart (Dave Foley) so they can sell the apartment for a higher price; Karen demands that Lyle (John Cleese) discipline his daughter (Minnie Driver).
Real estate entrepreneurs Will and Grace face formidable competition on the East Side from a lesbian couple (Edie Falco, Chloë Sevigny); John Edward gives Karen some psychic guidance.
Jack and Grace stumble upon Stuart (Dave Foley) watching a movie matinée in the company of another man; Will tries to teach Karen how to drive.
Grace advises Will to play hard to get with his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale); Jack and Karen despair after learning their favorite TV series will be going off the air.
Will introduces his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale) to overly critical Grace; Karen tells Jack that their friendship will change after her wedding.
At Tina's (Lesley Ann Warren) urging, Will tries to find out if there is a new woman in his father's life; Jack's son decides to try out for the high-school cheerleading squad.
On the eve of his graduation from nursing school, Jack turns to Will for help writing his commencement address.
Karen moves her wedding to Las Vegas, where Jennifer Lopez agrees to sing at the ceremony.
Karen recruits Jack to help her get Jennifer Lopez to listen to Karen's new song; Grace takes out her frustration over her cheating husband on Will.
Jack wangles his way into Janet Jackson's (guest starring as herself) performance tour as a backup dancer.
As she attempts to steal doughnuts at an AA meeting, Grace has a surprise reunion with Val (Molly Shannon); Will and Jack attend a gay television focus group meeting.
Grace accuses Will of being too nice to strangers; Jack has trouble at his new company when his co-workers mock him about his Cher doll.
Despite the fact that Will has never had a happy birthday, his new relationship with Vince (Bobby Cannavale) gives him hope that this one will be.
Will convinces Jack to aid a local gay-bookstore owner to save his store from closing.
Will and Grace decide to invite Vince and Nadine (Kristin Davis) over, but they quickly learn that, despite similarities in friendship, they are polar opposites.
After a great date with someone else, Grace comes home to a garbled message from Leo; Karen and Jack try to set each other up, but things go awry.
Will, Grace, Jack and Karen go on a road trip for Grace's getaway weekend, but Jack and Karen hate the car ride and bail on the plan.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.
Panic hits when Screech (Dustin Diamond) finds out he has to play a Russian exchange student in the chess finals. With Dennis Haskins.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).

The student council decides to hold a dance-date auction to raise money for new cheerleading uniforms.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) needs a high SAT score to achieve her dream of attending prestigious Stansbury University.
When a girl isn't allowed to try out for the wrestling team, the students band together and protest the decision.
Teenage movie star Johnny Dakota chooses Bayside as the site for an anti-drug commercial. With Mario Lopez and Dustin Diamond.
On Bayside's annual "cut school day," Mr. Belding warns Zack that if he is absent one more time he will be suspended.
Lisa and Screech make a "love machine" for their science project.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) latest moneymaking scheme involves a "Girls of Bayside" video-dating tape.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) does everything in her power to break up her father's wedding. With Dustin Diamond.
Everyone gets summer jobs at a fancy beach club and decides to hold Zack's birthday party there.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) promises Mr. Carosi (Ernie Sabella) the gang will win a volleyball game against a rival beach club.
Stacy (Leah Remini) gets confused after she enters a contest at Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) urging and finds that he voted for Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen).
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is in love with Stacy (Leah Remini) but fears she is only interested in her college boyfriend.
Stacy (Leah Remini), in charge of the club for the day, learns her father booked two parties for the same night. With Mario Lopez.
Stacy (Leah Remini) moves out after her father forbids her to see Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar).
The entire gang goes to the mall to obtain U2 tickets and ends up camping out overnight. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
Jessie's father invites everyone to his Palm Springs resort to attend his wedding. With Elizabeth Berkley and Mario Lopez.
Casey Kasem (guest starring as himself) chronicles the rise of the rock group Zack Attack. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
The students are shocked during the Christmas season to discover the new girl working in Mr. Moody's store is homeless.
Zack's family invites Laura and her father home for Christmas.
Lisa (Lark Voorhies) wins a mystery weekend at Mr. Jameson's mansion and invites the gang to participate. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) come to blows when they both fall for the new girl in their senior class.
For one week, the students switch places with the teachers, and Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes principal.
Screech (Dustin Diamond) is targeted by a gold digger when his spaghetti sauce business becomes a huge success.
The gang agrees to pitch in and stage a fashion show to exhibit Lisa's designs for a visiting fashion recruiter.
Slater can't find a way to tell his father that he doesn't want to go to West Point.
Valentine's Day finds the gang at the Max reminiscing about past relationships. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's plan to encourage the teachers to strike backfires on the students when the Academic Bowl is canceled.
The gang scrambles for dates as the senior prom approaches. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
A look into the future finds Belding with six students who are very similar to the gang from the class of 1993.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is desperate enough to try ballet class when he learns he needs one more credit to graduate.
Zack's partner for a school project is the new girl at Bayside, a tough biker who is not at all impressed with him.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes overprotective of the physically challenged girl he is counseling on the teen line.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) bet to see who can kiss Tori (Leanna Creel) first.
Zack tries to sneak out of detention so he can participate in a contest that has a trip to Hawaii as the prize.
Slater, Lisa, Zack and Screech (Mario Lopez, Lark Voorhies, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Dustin Diamond) are involved in a drunken driving accident.
Zack talks everyone into buying class rings from a man named Gem Diamond.
The guys and the girls stage a competition to decide who gets to spend a $10,000 inheritance. With Lark Voorhies and Dustin Diamond.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) dates Slater's sister despite his friend's nervousness about the matter. With Mario Lopez.
Mrs. Belding (guest star Louan Gideon) goes into labor while trapped in an elevator with Zack and Tori (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Leanna Creel).
Zack, Slater, Screech and Lisa (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez, Dustin Diamond, Lark Voorhies) reflect on the summer they spent at Malibu Sands.
Zack enters a contest to write a new school song and resorts to sabotage.
Zack's summer romance with an older woman comes to a halt when she discovers he lied to her.
Zack promises to help Screech get a date with Lisa if Screech will do Zack's term paper.
Zack tries to cash in on a stock-market investment to get money to replace his father's video recorder.
A student opposed to killing animals for experiments releases all the science class frogs.
Zack's father falls for Miss Bliss.
Screech finds that an intimidating student has a learning disability.
Zack and a classmate ask the same girl to an upcoming dance, jeopardizing their friendship.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) scheme to get more time to study for a midterm ends up hurting his teacher. With Dennis Haskins.
A student argument helps a teacher resolve a problem with a longtime friend. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
A teacher turns a practical joke into a lesson about the criminal justice system. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to steal a kiss from a returning former student who is now a famous rock star.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is offered a chance to join a popular club. With Dustin Diamond.
A retired teacher with unorthodox methods stimulates the class when he substitutes for their regular teacher.
The gang enters a dance contest being held at the Max and hosted by radio personality Casey Kasem. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Lisa's (Lark Voorhies) friends invent ways to pay the bills she has accrued on her father's credit card. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
A freak lightning accident enables Screech (Dustin Diamond) to predict the future. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mario Lopez.
The guys hide a microphone at the girls' party to find out whom Kelly will ask to the dance.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) gets into unusual circumstances and clothes when he tries to help Screech (Dustin Diamond) get a date.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plan to get rid of Slater (Mario Lopez) backfires; Slater's revenge ends up benefiting Screech (Dustin Diamond).
When Ms. Simpson injures her back, a substitute teacher named Tony Crane takes over her class at Bayside; when all the girls fall for Mr. Crane, Zack and Slater become jealous.
When Kelly is nominated as homecoming queen, her dream is shattered as she faces the prospect of winning after she gets a zit; Zack comes up with a solution, but it does not unfold as he plans.

Matt LeBlanc, Chris Harris, and Rory Reid test the latest SUVs through the medium of horse trialing; Chris gets an explosive drive in the new Alpine A110; Jason Manford is the studio guest.

Jeremy Clarkson makes a film about the BMW X6 and ends up conducting one of the most expensive road tests in "Top Gear" history; James May drives the new Vauxhall Insignia VXR; Richard Hammond tests the Lexus supercar.
The guys test dog against machine.

Jeremy, Richard and James find a trio of cars which are equally at home on the racetrack as they are at transporting a family to the store.
The cars put to the test include the Aston Martin Rapide, the Porsche Panamera Turbo and the Maserati Quattroporte in a search for the world's greatest four seat supercar.
The boys build cool and interesting motor homes before setting off for a holiday weekend in the West country.
Richard takes the Volkswagen Touareg 4x4 to Sweden; Tom Cruise and Cameron Diaz are the "Stars in a Reasonably Priced Car."

Freddie tries to bungee-jump a car off a dam; Paddy sets out to prove an old hearse is the ultimate family car; Chris remembers the Lotus 79 race car.

Chris, Freddie and Paddy set out to turn an old hearse into the ultimate family car; Chris gets to grips with the lightweight Dallara Stradale; Zara and Mike Tindall go head-to-head in the Reasonably Fast Car.

Paddy McGuinness builds his own luxurious off-roader in the shape of the Dirty Rascal; Chris samples the Rolls-Royce Cullinan.

Hardie has trouble with his brother.
Hardie interviews job applicants.
Hardie searches for Eli Fisher, but first must deal with the man who's been trailing him -- and who's also searching for Fisher.
While in search of a thief called The Utah Kid, Jim learns that his quarry has been hanged in a small town -- but the crook's stolen cash remains missing.
Hardie suspects that a paroled man -- who is working as an eccentric frontier dentist -- may have something to do with a murdered stage driver.
Hardie is chasing down a suspect wanted for robbery and murder, but a town sheriff's ties to the suspect's family might make matters difficult.
A jewel shipment must be delivered, and the owner's daughter wants to do it personally.
A judge notorious for going strictly by the book in his effort to bring order to the frontier faces the ultimate test when his son finds himself in court.
A sergeant looking to kill two deserters drags a fresh young lieutenant along on his vendetta and mistakes Chris for one of his targets.
Chris and Duke try to rush a group to California despite inclement weather; Duke injures his foot, forcing him off the trail and into a cabin to heal up.

While on a scouting mission, Flint is stopped by a scavenger who tries to detour the wagon train into the path of a hidden cannon by saying that he has blasted a road through a dead end canyon that will save the train two weeks.
A teacher traveling with the wagon train encounters conflict when he becomes attracted to the daughter of a preacher who has just joined the train.
An ousted medicine man predicts the future of a wagon train passenger.
Flint leads a fragment of the wagon train on a dangerous route through a swamp that supposedly contains mysterious creatures.
While crossing a sprawling ranch, trouble brews between two newlyweds and an interloper.
Chris Hale is traveling to see his brother Levi, who's about to be released from prison.
When an antisocial father and son join the wagon train, their problematic relationship leads one woman to believe the son is being abused.
Bill Hawks shoots a horse thief and later discovers the man was already declared dead as a war hero.
A Frenchman arouses strong, and polarized, emotions among the wagoners; men distrust him, women adore him.
Injured on the trail, Jess is found by an old friend who has been rustling cattle in the area, and finds himself mistaken for one of the rustlers.
Shooters from miles around gather in Laramie for the annual Sunday Shoot, but when some disagree with the outcome, Slim and Jess step in.
Outlaws who rob and then kill a wealthy rancher find their escape is slowed when their booty -- weighty gold coins -- becomes difficult to transport.
Some women suffragettes arrive in Laramie, and Daisy invites two of them to dinner at the ranch, though Slim and the leader of the group don't see eye to eye.
When a young woman dies at the ranch, Jess escorts her son to his father, unaware that the mother wanted the boy to go to her sister in Denver.
When $50,000 goes missing from a stagecoach, and with few leads to go on, Jim suspects a safe-cracking marshal of the theft.

Hardie is transporting a prisoner to stand trial in Santa Fe, but when they stop in a small town along the way, he discovers that there's a price on the man's head -- and the mayor and sheriff may not let him leave alive.
A stolen stagecoach is found by Hardie in a town near the Mexico border, miles from any Wells Fargo station.
The murder of a casino manager.
A vengeful woman informs Hardie of a plot to rob a Wells Fargo station.
Hardie and an old friend track down a suspect who might know the location of Jefferson Davis' buried treasure.
Jim learns that his friend's fiancée holds the key to finding a stagecoach bandit.
An outlaw poses as an Army major.
Hardie wonders why a prisoner acts unconcerned about his coming murder trial.
Hardie sets out to capture gunrunners.
An Army captain wanted for desertion.
An actor visits a ghost town where he last appeared with his late wife.
Hardie faces opposition when he tries to investigate a friend's drowning death.
A Wells Fargo employee has been killed and Hardie suspects a boxer.
An incoming stage has problems with a drunken, violent passenger who turns out to be the boxer John L. Sullivan.
Hardie becomes involved with a female Wells Fargo agent.
Hardie gets assigned to protect a diamond salesman carrying a small fortune in gems.
Flint happens to learn the whereabouts of a man he's been hunting for years to kill.
Duke's resemblance to gambler Jason Carter makes him the target for a murderer's bullet.
Bill and Charlie help an old friend, John Turnbull, defend his reservation against local land sharks who look to initiate a range war.
Duke takes a job as a deputy under Hiram Winthrop, a man who wants to teach farming to the Apache.
After being shot in a holdup, a bank robber unknowingly receives the wrong medicine from an old pharmacist.
A sheriff believes a woman (June Walker) is guilty of her husband's murder but has no evidence. With Ann Harding and Frances Reid.
A woman has second thoughts about marriage when her future husband lectures her about indiscretions and torture.
A struggling actor invites a fellow actor to his apartment to rehearse a role for which they are competing.
A policeman working the night shift encounters an old man with amnesia (Claude Rains) and a lost boy (Bill Mumy).
Taking advantage of his girlfriend's job at a psychiatrist's office, a small-time crook cooks up a lucrative money-making scheme.
A man's (Andrew Prine) confidence in a faith healer (Sidney Blackmer) leads to an interesting situation for both of them. With Maggie Pierce and Robert Armstrong.
In his run from the law, an escaped convict kidnaps a young woman, unaware of her relationship to his latest victim.
Following a train accident, a man plans to cheat an insurance company out of a large amount of money.
Following the close of a murder trial, an attorney continues to seek the truth for his own personal satisfaction.
On the verge of losing his job, an advertising executive is desperate to come up with a successful ad campaign.
A gang of teen thieves hits one house too many when they target a mob gangster's (Philip Reed) home. With Tom Gilleran and Rafael Campos.
A retired man plans to run away with his mistress and stolen company funds, but his wife has something else in mind.
A man and his lover (Mark Miller, Patricia Breslin) plot to eliminate his wife (Vivienne Segal) so they can be together.
An undertaker (John Fielder) attempts to collect from a penny-pinching killer (Ed Gardner).
A seedy character (Frankie Darro) discovers an amazing formula and decides to use it to make some quick cash. With Robert Keith and Karl Lukas.
A man's (Gene Evans) obsession over his pet dog pushes him over the edge when the dog suddenly dies. With Carmen Mathews.
A jewelry shop owner sells a rare black pearl to a client, who later returns looking for another one to make a matched pair.
A television writer tries to protect a young woman from an older man who wants to marry her; a hitchhiking teen leads a TV writer to a motel owner who would kill to get into show business.
A depressed man's life changes when he falls for a working guest at a suicide club.
A man's childhood nanny begins to act suspiciously after he hires her to care for his baby.
An overlooked, unlocked cellar window leads to terror when an escaped, insane killer is on the loose.
Peg is bored with her marriage to Ted, a wealthy toy manufacturer; she seizes a golden opportunity to eliminate her husband.
An ordinary man discovers adding a toupee and a beard to change his appearance causes more problems than he anticipated.
A once-prominent Hollywood family discovers a way to improve finances. With John Carradine, Vera Miles, James Farentino.
Having had a bad run of luck, a man (Howard Morris) tracks down an old college friend (Jack Carter) in hopes of landing a job.
A husband searches desperately for his wife in a neighborhood where numerous murders have been committed.
A shoplifter (Coleen Gray) is blackmailed into helping the store manager (Richard Long) in a crime of his own.
A meek clerk (Dick York) plots with his associates to rob their investment firm. With Wendell Holmes.
A wanted man (Jack Carson) disappears while visiting a little-known tourist attraction in Italy. With Christopher Dark.
A recently-divorced man (Robert Webber) makes a deal with a friend (Jeremy Slate) to avoid having to pay alimony.
A man (Wayne Rogers) decides to demonstrate to his new-found girlfriend (Anne Helm) how he gets his kicks. With Brian Hutton.
A housekeeper make arrangements to keep her lover all to herself when he expresses interest in another woman.
A woman (Linda Purl) is attacked in her home and her husband (David Clennon) takes the law into his own hands.
Two retired insurance salesmen (Robert H. Harris, John Qualen) expect murder when the temperature reaches 92 degrees.
A young man (John Forsythe) returns home after an absence of four years to investigate his father's death.
A woman (Ellen Corby) tries to prevent a shootout between two gunslingers (Darren McGavin, Gene Barry).
A determined detective (Robert Emhardt) uncovers a man's scheme to have his "missing" wife declared legally dead.
A woman (Patricia Hitchcock) visiting Paris returns to her hotel room to find her ailing mother missing.
A gangster (Gene Barry) plans to punish the woman (Nancy Gates) he feels is responsible for his brother's death.
A businessman, injured in a car crash and believed by everyone to be dead, fights to signal he is alive.
A man (Everett Sloane) suspects his cook (Beulah Bondi) of being an arsenic-poisoning murderer. With Janet Ward.
A down-on-his-luck man responds to a newspaper ad from a man seeking a companion for a cross-country trip.
A man (Tom Ewell) believes an exact double is gradually taking over his life.
A woman (Judith Evelyn) is suspected of murdering her husband, who has been having an affair with another woman. With Joe Mantell and Kathleen McGuire.
A larcenous store Santa (Barry Fitzgerald) helps change the ways of a potential delinquent (Bobby Clark).
A man (Darren McGavin) tries to trick an elderly woman (Patricia Collinge) out of a family heirloom.
A man (John Qualen) is surprised to learn that the boss he thought he had murdered is still alive. With Philip Reed.
A gunman (George Mathews), intent on murdering his girlfriend, purchases an alibi.
An escaped convict (John Cassavetes) takes refuge in a farmhouse occupied by a young housewife (Marisa Pavan).
A year after the murders, a newspaper reporter (Joan Lorring) attempts to interview Lizzie Borden (Carmen Mathews) and her sister about the killings.
A bum (Robert Newton) witnesses a murder and decide to take advantage of the situation. With Philip Reed.
A police detective (Charles Bronson) investigating a murder focuses on a strange ventriloquist (Claude Rains).
A female reporter (Claire Trevor) encounters problem trying to leave Eastern Europe after meeting a soccer star.
A man (Mark Damon) arrives at a monastery bent on revenge and is convinced by a kind priest (Everett Sloane) to mend his heart.
An English man (John Williams) murders his wife and moves to California, thinking he has committed the perfect crime.
Two greedy brothers plan to murder their elderly aunt (Mildred Natwick) in an attempt to inherit her money.
A desperate couple (Charles Bronson, Norma Crane) plans to rob an eccentric old woman (Estelle Winwood).
An angel (Alan Napier) allows a murdered mystery writer (John Williams) to return to Earth to uncover his killer.

Eddie announces he is quitting school.
Unbeknownst to their parents, Wally stays overnight at Lumpy's and Beaver's friend stays overnight with him.

Beaver becomes the last-minute replacement for Wally on a baby-sitting job.
Beaver tries to live up to Wally's reputation when he joins a basketball team.
Beaver convinces Ward to buy typewriter.
Ward and June fear that Wally wants to join the Merchant Marine.
Girl whom Beaver likes falls for Wally.
Wally and Beaver are told they must clean up the yard before they can leave for the day.

Wally and Eddie are invited to join an exclusive social club.

Lumpy and Eddie go camping with Beaver.
Beaver and his friends make a long-distance call to a baseball player.
Wally and Beaver learn a lesson in economics when they invest in the stock market.
Wally receives permission to stay home during his family's annual vacation.
Wally forgets his wallet on a date.
Beaver is the only one among his friends to honor a pact to dress casually for an awards dinner.
